title: OurApp_vs_Obsidian
scope: All identified MyNotes functional families and all 29 internal Obsidian modules in the retained pinned-version registry; not all possible third-party extensions or full functional acceptance.
method: Visual expert inspection of retained native frames (additional contact-sheet review) plus bounded implementation and provenance review. No new live/device/participant session.

modules.title: Find, organise, label and reorder
modules.scope: Search, folders, labels/tags, list/grid, sorting and manual order
modules.observed: The retained home has a floating New note overlapping preview words; Library combines destinations and creation actions. Current source makes a nonempty home query global, bypassing the current folder/workspace/label filters.
modules.comparison: Quick switcher, file explorer, tags and full-content search are distinct Obsidian surfaces. Its empty search frame does not demonstrate better relevance or speed.
modules.judgment: Priority remains content visibility and a clearly stated search contract. Detailed findings N01–N10 are retained in the phase-one appendix.
modules.direction: Keep floating creation and cross-workspace search, but state scope and protect preview space; separate browsing from administration.
modules.task: Find an archived body-only match while a folder filter is active; reorder a distant card, then return.
modules.acceptance: Record actual scope, result passage, selected filters and persisted order; repeat list/grid, keyboard and large text. Measure drag continuity only in a new live session.

modules.title: Writing, reading and formatting
modules.scope: Notes/Doc, selected text, new typing, headings and Markdown modes
modules.observed: Format plus keyboard leaves only a short strip of writing context. The source already has selected-text/new-typing semantics and accessible selected controls; formatting is not declared broken.
modules.comparison: Obsidian keeps a compact keyboard toolbar but exposes Markdown syntax and icon-learning costs. It is not automatically simpler for a novice.
modules.judgment: E01–E10 in the appendix explain context, hierarchy and feedback problems. More controls are not a substitute for confident writing.
modules.direction: Adapt the existing single Format panel to the available viewport; preserve labels, selection, fifth Clear and direct editing.
modules.task: Format the middle of a paragraph, type new text, undo, dismiss the keyboard and reopen the note.
modules.acceptance: Retain surrounding prose, correct style target, caret and saved result. Repeat with large text; compare actual task completion and mistakes, not assertion counts.

modules.title: Checklists, numbering and list editing
modules.scope: Complete, indent, reorder, convert selected text and hide checked
modules.observed: Our row sheet labels its target List item 1 and exposes Indent/Outdent/Remove; checklist-level actions occupy another sheet. That helps discoverability but requires understanding row versus whole-list scope.
modules.comparison: Obsidian renders bullets, numbered items and checkboxes inside prose. The retained transformation readbacks establish narrow Markdown edits, not equal drag usability.
modules.judgment: Candidate friction is scope switching, not an established inability to edit lists. Do not remove our visible text labels just to imitate Markdown.
modules.direction: Keep row grips, direct item insertion, named lists and a non-drag Move route; make the affected list/item unmistakable.
modules.task: Insert an item in the middle, indent it, move it past the viewport, hide completed rows and undo.
modules.acceptance: No lost items, wrong-list operations or accidental workspace swipes. Verify numbering after insertion and Backspace exit at an empty item.

modules.title: Tables and direct cell editing
modules.scope: Cell/row/column operations, header role and wide content
modules.observed: Our table is embedded with a named-content header and nearby pen/overflow actions. The captured compact table does not establish behavior for many columns, large fonts or long cells.
modules.comparison: Obsidian shows a readable rendered Markdown table; that is not evidence its cell editor, paste or column operations are faster.
modules.judgment: Scope ambiguity and narrow-screen navigation need validation. E08 already flags multiple neighboring action scopes.
modules.direction: Preserve direct cell editing, header toggles, boundaries, overflow cues and undoable confirmed deletion.
modules.task: Edit a long cell in a wide table; insert a column beside it, toggle header role, delete a row and undo.
modules.acceptance: Keep the active cell visible above the IME; no unexpected horizontal jump; restore content and header meaning after undo. Compare the same table, not these unequal fixtures.

modules.title: Images, attachments and inline media
modules.scope: Insert, name, select, crop/edit, remove and return to text
modules.observed: Our image selection sheet presents Use text, Keep image, Read this area and selection controls together. This is a specialised workflow with several possible outcomes to interpret.
modules.comparison: Obsidian captures links and an embedded note. This is not a matched image crop or OCR interface, and media/PDF embed correctness was not functionally accepted.
modules.judgment: Candidate mental-model friction: selecting an image region, extracting words and editing an attachment must not appear to be the same destructive operation.
modules.direction: Explain what each action inserts or retains, preserve originals, and keep image management subordinate to reading.
modules.task: Insert a photo, select two recognized words, keep the image, edit its crop, then remove only the intended attachment.
modules.acceptance: Keep source bytes, unrelated blocks and names intact; make copy versus replacement clear. Verify offscreen word selection and explicit outside-tap dismissal.

modules.title: Web hyperlinks and external opening
modules.scope: Display text, safe URL validation, edit/remove and browser consent
modules.observed: Our Hyperlink form separates display text and address; the captured invalid-address state shows an error affordance. Source limits web links to HTTP/HTTPS and confirms external opening.
modules.comparison: Obsidian internal links and embeds are not the same operation as adding a web URL. Do not award a graph/navigation win for a web-link form.
modules.judgment: Validation visibility and multiline entry deserve a matched test; no claim of broken link handling follows from this captured fixture.
modules.direction: Keep visible URL errors and original words on Remove; identify when another app will open.
modules.task: Add a long URL to selected words, correct a malformed address, reopen, edit and remove the link.
modules.acceptance: No duplicate URL per line, changed neighboring prose or unnoticed external launch. Check keyboard visibility, wrapped fields and TalkBack error announcement.

modules.title: Internal links, backlinks, graph and previews
modules.scope: Connected-note navigation and local/global context
modules.observed: The scoped MyNotes source inspection establishes web links; it does not establish an equivalent vault-wide internal-link/backlink/graph workflow. This is a candidate scope gap, not a proved app-wide absence.
modules.comparison: Obsidian shows linked mentions with a passage, outgoing links, global/local graphs and an embedded note. A tiny graph with a large options panel also has cognitive and viewport costs.
modules.judgment: Potential effectiveness gap for connected research notes, not a reason to add a decorative graph to every simple note.
modules.direction: Validate whether users need stable internal-note references first. Prefer a small reliable related-note route before copying complex graph controls.
modules.task: Link A to a heading in B, rename B, return through backlinks and preview the target without losing A.
modules.acceptance: Target identity and rename behavior must be verified live; count wrong destinations and recovery steps. No graph speed or link-integrity winner has been measured.

modules.title: Long-note orientation, tags, footnotes and word count
modules.scope: Headings, jump/navigation, find and document context
modules.observed: MyNotes supports headings and highlighted find return. The reviewed source/captures do not establish a heading-outline jump path equivalent to the captured Obsidian outline.
modules.comparison: Obsidian tags and outline are visible; the Footnotes pane says No footnotes found even though fixture text contains a footnote. Rendered detection was explicitly blocked, not accepted.
modules.judgment: Long-note orientation is a candidate gap; footnote and word-count completeness remain untested in our matching scope.
modules.direction: Keep fast highlighted Find, and validate a compact heading route rather than adding permanent chrome.
modules.task: Locate a middle heading, find a repeated phrase, follow a footnote and return to the exact reading location.
modules.acceptance: Verify target and return anchors, heading levels, counts and generated text treatment; do not infer footnote success from a registered command.

modules.title: Properties and Bases
modules.scope: Structured metadata, records and filtered views
modules.observed: Our note properties include labels, color, folder and reminder state; arbitrary typed-property and database-view editing is not established by this inspection.
modules.comparison: Obsidian shows typed properties and a Bases table of vault files. The canonical standalone Properties attempt was obscured; visible Properties is a layout reference, not proof of a successful properties interaction.
modules.judgment: Not a fair row-for-row comparison with our document tables. A Bases database is a different information architecture, not just more columns.
modules.direction: Treat structured-record management as a separate product decision. Do not burden everyday notes with unused metadata fields.
modules.task: For users who need records, edit one typed field, filter a view, rename a file and reopen the view.
modules.acceptance: Validate data types, retained filters, note identity and error recovery. No Bases performance, formulas or equivalent MyNotes capability is certified here.

modules.title: Quick capture, daily notes, templates and unique notes
modules.scope: Start a useful note with low setup cost
modules.observed: Our floating create action is direct, but a sparse fixture cannot establish first-use usefulness. The reviewed slice does not establish equivalent daily-note/template workflows.
modules.comparison: Obsidian daily notes and timestamp names are visible. Template insertion failed because no template folder was configured; random-note invocation does not certify selection distribution.
modules.judgment: Capture efficiency is a shared job; daily notes/templates are optional aids, not automatic points. Setup failures must not be presented as competitor success.
modules.direction: Preserve immediate blank-note creation. Evaluate templates only against actual repeated writing tasks and explain required configuration.
modules.task: From a cold start, capture a short thought; then create a repeated meeting structure and return tomorrow.
modules.acceptance: Observe time to first saved words, setup mistakes, duplicate daily notes and return continuity. Do not populate fake user content to make the app feel busy.
modules.kind: Shared capture task / optional workflows unknown

modules.title: Freehand drawing and Canvas
modules.scope: Visual thinking, embedded drawings versus spatial boards
modules.observed: Our dedicated drawing screen exposes labelled Pen/Pencil/Highlighter, width/color and undo tools; the frame alone does not measure pen latency, palm rejection or save reliability.
modules.comparison: Obsidian Canvas shows connected cards on a spatial board. It is not a native freehand drawing benchmark, and the requested landscape captures stayed portrait.
modules.judgment: These tools overlap in visual thinking but are not interchangeable. Do not score our pen tools against a card-board feature count.
modules.direction: Keep accessible drawing tools and clear draft/save meaning; make the transition back to the containing note predictable.
modules.task: Draw a diagram annotation, leave and reopen it; in Canvas connect two cards, pan/zoom and reopen the board.
modules.acceptance: Evaluate each tool against its own output goal. For common save/return work, preserve content and location; latency needs real stroke traces on matched hardware.

modules.title: Diagrams, shapes, arrows and grouping
modules.scope: Create/edit a bounded structured visual
modules.observed: Our diagram editor has shape selection plus a separate options sheet for Group shapes, Edit arrows and Split arrow. A large empty canvas in a one-shape fixture is not evidence of missing content.
modules.comparison: Canvas is the nearest retained Obsidian visual reference, not a matched shape-and-arrow editor. No successful comparator arrow/group gesture is established.
modules.judgment: Candidate discoverability issue: users must find contextual grouping and connection actions without confusing selection, editing and export.
modules.direction: Preserve colorless diagram options, pen-scoped names and direct arrow editing. Improve guidance at the relevant selection state, not with a permanent tutorial overlay.
modules.task: Add two shapes, connect them, group, resize, split the arrow, undo and reopen.
modules.acceptance: Check actual anchor geometry, target selection, retained names and no accidental duplication. Run long-press/context-menu actions with large text and TalkBack.

modules.title: PDF reading, selection, search and markup
modules.scope: Open, scroll, zoom, find, annotate and export a marked copy
modules.observed: Current retained frames show a compact filename toolbar, keyboard-adjacent find field and separate markup rail. Earlier rejected viewer duplication should not be reported as still present.
modules.comparison: The Obsidian audit did not certify PDF embed/viewer workflows. No matched PDF search, annotation or original-preservation run exists for it.
modules.judgment: Current design has the requested shape; gesture precision, search latency, scrubber timeout and zoom continuity remain acceptance work, not proved polish.
modules.direction: Retain real file-wide zoom, selection-clearing outside tap, compact controls, loader and the hiding page scrubber. Do not reintroduce Go to page or duplicate counts.
modules.task: Open a large scanned/mixed PDF, zoom a distant page, select offscreen text, find a hit with IME, mark a rotated page and export.
modules.acceptance: Compare the original bytes; inspect hit position, highlight geometry and rendered export. Exercise cancellation and a partial destination; private markup drafts are outside Notes backups.

modules.title: Word files and original-layout expectations
modules.scope: DOCX preview, selection, zoom, import versus original reader
modules.observed: Our filename toolbar is compact. Source explicitly says MyNotes pages are an approximate local preview and offers an original-layout reader or a separate editable copy.
modules.comparison: Obsidian is not a retained Word-layout comparator; its rendered Markdown cannot establish DOCX fidelity.
modules.judgment: Effectiveness depends on honest mode boundaries. A readable preview must not be mistaken for a faithful Office renderer or editable original.
modules.direction: Keep the original-only opening flow and clear disclosure. Separate page appearance controls from edits to imported content.
modules.task: Open a DOCX with headers, inline images, wide tables and hard page breaks; select text, zoom and create an editable copy.
modules.acceptance: Check original bytes and document return position, compare rendered pages with a suitable Word reference, and disclose any dropped layout/media. Do not invent fidelity from a synthetic one-page frame.

modules.title: Large TXT and read-only text viewing
modules.scope: Pagination, selecting, find and creating an explicit editable copy
modules.observed: Our retained TXT view shows real text, a 1/17 page indicator and page arrows rather than the note editor. It is an opening state, not a measured large-file completion test.
modules.comparison: Obsidian native Markdown reading is a text-oriented reference, but arbitrary TXT opening, pagination and selection were not matched.
modules.judgment: The shared job is locating and copying information without accidentally importing or overwriting the source. Input size alone is not proof of low latency.
modules.direction: Preserve read-only original viewing until explicit copy/edit, and stable search/selection across page boundaries.
modules.task: Open a large multilingual TXT, find a repeated phrase near the end, select across the viewport and return to the prior file list.
modules.acceptance: Measure open/find latency separately from rendering; inspect Unicode integrity, clear selection on deliberate tap, retained page and unchanged original.

modules.title: Spreadsheet previews and cached values
modules.scope: CSV/XLSX grids, viewport navigation and data expectations
modules.observed: Our preview exposes a 3-row, 2-column fixture with row/column coordinates. The inspected source opens CSV/XLSX through SpreadsheetFile and SpreadsheetPreview.
modules.comparison: Obsidian Bases is a vault-record view, not an Excel engine. Its table cannot establish XLSX formula execution, workbook fidelity or CSV compatibility.
modules.judgment: Do not imply a preview is a full spreadsheet editor. Cached-value handling and sheet ordering must be explained when creating text copies.
modules.direction: Keep grid context and explicit preview mode; provide readable wide-cell navigation without competing zoom/scroll gestures.
modules.task: Open quoted CSV and a multi-sheet XLSX with formulas, missing cached results and wide cells; locate a value and copy it.
modules.acceptance: Compare visible rows/columns and Unicode with source values, disclose cached-only results, retain sheet/scroll position and never execute macros or scripts.

modules.title: Markdown, HTML, RTF, ODT and slide imports
modules.scope: Safe text extraction versus native rich rendering
modules.observed: CommonFileText supports CSV/Markdown/HTML/RTF/ODT/XLSX/PPTX extraction. HTML strips script/style blocks; Office extraction does not promise layout, media or live formulas.
modules.comparison: Obsidian natively renders Markdown with code/callouts/math. This is not proof of equivalent import behavior for every other file type.
modules.judgment: Our supported-extension breadth should not hide a lower-fidelity text-copy contract. This is a source-supported limitation, not a reproduced corruption bug.
modules.direction: Explain exactly what a viewer preserves and what an editable copy drops before confirmation; keep other-reader privacy boundaries explicit.
modules.task: Open one realistic file of each advertised type, inspect text order and unsupported elements, then cancel or create a copy.
modules.acceptance: Record per-format fidelity and actionable errors; preserve originals, reject malformed/oversized archives safely and distinguish external-reader delegation from in-app support.

modules.title: OCR, image-region text and scanned-page recognition
modules.scope: English/Hindi/Kannada, correction, provenance and loaders
modules.observed: The retained review screen requires checking text before saving. The delivered qualification receipt says OCR targets were met for 1512/1536 main observations; eight extra public scenes executed with zero exact outputs.
modules.comparison: No equivalent built-in Obsidian OCR outcome was established. A denied/absent comparator workflow is not an accuracy win for us.
modules.judgment: Known recognition-quality limit, not merely a styling concern. Generated repeated-reference observations do not establish field accuracy on varied posters, tiny fonts or emoji.
modules.direction: Keep original images, explicit user-triggered OCR, visible loading, editable review and a clear insertion destination. Do not silently retry duplicates or invent unsupported-language text.
modules.task: Read tiny/oblique/multilingual public scenes, blank controls and selected image regions; compare exact expected text and corrected output.
modules.acceptance: Retain source hashes, full hypotheses, CER, omissions/false words, cold/warm latency and correction time. No new accuracy study or training occurred in this report.
modules.kind: Retained measured limitation, not new live reproduction

modules.title: Voice recording, playback and transcription
modules.scope: Permission, pause/resume, originals, review and speech engines
modules.observed: Our inbox displays transcript state, playback controls and a progress rail. Existing qualification met speech targets for 2528/3216 observations, not all. The optional engine is labelled experimental.
modules.comparison: Obsidian audio recorder reached permission denial in its audit; successful recording, playback and quality were not certified. Recording audio is not equivalent to transcription.
modules.judgment: Known effectiveness limits must not be buried behind a polished inbox. Neither a playback icon nor an aggregate processing rate proves physical listening quality.
modules.direction: Preserve original audio independently of transcripts, honest engine labels, readable progress and review-before-use. Do not claim general Indian-accent competence from one adapted speaker.
modules.task: Record varied Indian speakers, pause/resume, deny/regrant permission, play through a headset and correct names/numbers while listening.
modules.acceptance: Measure word errors, boundary losses, time-to-review, seek accuracy and actual audible playback on physical hardware. Verify originals export separately from note backups.
modules.kind: Retained accuracy limitation / comparator recording blocked

modules.title: Reminders and notifications
modules.scope: Schedule, rename, deliver, cancel and reopen the intended note
modules.observed: A native time picker is visible. LocalReminders schedules inexact alarms and checks notification permission/channel state; this is not proof that a reminder arrived on a physical device.
modules.comparison: Daily-note creation in Obsidian is not equivalent to notification scheduling. No built-in matched reminder-delivery workflow is established.
modules.judgment: Delivery expectation is the key effectiveness risk: a selected time must not imply an exact-alarm guarantee the implementation does not provide.
modules.direction: Keep reminders optional, renameable and local; explain approximate timing and permission blocks at the point they matter.
modules.task: Set, rename and reschedule a reminder, deny notifications, reboot and then tap the delivered notification.
modules.acceptance: Use disposable notes; verify no stale/duplicate notification, correct note identity and sensible blocked-state feedback. Measure actual delivery under power restrictions separately.

modules.title: Home widget and Android entry points
modules.scope: Pinned/recent projection, resizing, share-in and deep-link continuity
modules.observed: Settings offers a Home widget. NotesWidget source renders up to four projected note titles and a first-use empty message; no launcher widget screenshot is used as visual acceptance evidence.
modules.comparison: The retained Obsidian mobile quick action is an in-app gesture, not proof of an equivalent Android home widget.
modules.judgment: Source presence is not launcher usability. Actual widget placement, refresh and accessibility are outstanding.
modules.direction: Preserve optional widget consent, pinned-first content and clear launch destinations; do not expose trashed notes through stale OS surfaces.
modules.task: Place/resize the widget, pin and archive notes, share text from another app and open a reminder deep link.
modules.acceptance: Verify labels, intended note, no duplicates and return context on real launchers, including large system text. Do not restore widget/notification consent silently during recovery.
modules.kind: Source inspection only for launcher workflow

modules.title: Appearance, backgrounds, fonts and accessibility
modules.scope: Theme, paper, writing lines, large text and assistive input
modules.observed: Our theme sheet has System/Light/Dark choices, while note paper backgrounds and text formatting are separate controls. E04 already notes implementation-facing sp units; Obsidian also exposes pixels.
modules.comparison: Obsidian offers base scheme, accent, themes, fonts and CSS snippets. More appearance settings do not prove better contrast, legibility or accessible interaction.
modules.judgment: Potential confusion comes from several appearance scopes and cramped large-text editing, not a lack of decorative options.
modules.direction: Preserve system appearance, legible labels, writing-line independence and generous targets; clarify app theme versus note paper versus selected-text color.
modules.task: Switch system theme, increase font scale, navigate with TalkBack and format selected text over a patterned background.
modules.acceptance: Check clipping, announced scope/selection, contrast and focus order across orientations; screenshots alone do not establish 48dp targets or a successful screen-reader task.

modules.title: First-use storage, private folders and optional App folder
modules.scope: Where notes live, extra copies, reconnect and recovery expectations
modules.observed: Our Storage & recovery page explains on-phone saving plus optional extra copies. A second dialog lists selectable categories and says active recording remains pending until stopped.
modules.comparison: Obsidian audit used private app storage; its vault is not an automatic cross-device backup. Private app storage is vulnerable to uninstall in both workflows.
modules.judgment: Our architecture asks users to distinguish private notes, organisational folders, extra App-folder copies and portable backup. This is a real mental-model burden, not evidence of current data loss.
modules.direction: Keep truthful copy/permission warnings but use progressive disclosure and one understandable status: saved privately, extra copy ready/pending, recovery needs verification.
modules.task: Create notes offline, choose an empty optional folder, revoke access, save again and reconnect without clearing app data.
modules.acceptance: Inspect exact copied categories and pending status; test reinstall/reselection only on disposable fixtures. Never tell the user to uninstall or clear their real library for this review.

modules.title: Portable backup, import merge and full recovery
modules.scope: Verify output, disclose exclusions, restore without overwriting newer work
modules.observed: The backup page visibly lists exclusions; restore previews added/skipped/conflicting notes before Confirm merge. BackupCodec and the UI explicitly cap portable backup at 8 MiB.
modules.comparison: Obsidian file recovery is per-file history, not a certified full-vault backup/restore path. Sync is not used here as a backup benchmark.
modules.judgment: The 8 MiB bound is a concrete portability limitation for rich libraries. Original audio, empty folders, saved named presets and edit history are excluded; private PDF drafts need separate export.
modules.direction: Make backup scope and actual readiness legible before users rely on it. Preserve checksum/readback, non-destructive merge and checkpoints; plan larger-library portability only after comparison approval.
modules.task: Export a near-limit rich library, exceed the limit safely, import identical and same-ID changed notes, then verify every supported content type.
modules.acceptance: No silent partial success or overwrite; disclose omitted categories and readable/non-encrypted JSON. A complete App-folder checkpoint is a separate opt-in recovery mechanism, not this portable file.

modules.title: Trash, permanent deletion and recovery
modules.scope: Restore, seven-day retention policy, purge scope and safety
modules.observed: Our confirmation explicitly says permanent deletion cannot be undone and that backups/original voice recordings are kept separately. The ordinary Trash view lists deleted note cards.
modules.comparison: Obsidian local recovery shows source text with Copy/Restore actions. It is not a matched Trash purge or successful restoration test.
modules.judgment: The visible warning is a strength to preserve. Recovery confidence still depends on explaining different lifetimes for a note, recording, backup and annotation draft.
modules.direction: Keep seven-day Trash/Undo and explicit destructive confirmation. Make restoration and separately retained copies understandable without alarming first-use notes.
modules.task: Delete/restore a rich note, inspect what happens to its audio and exports, then purge only a disposable selected note.
modules.acceptance: Verify the exact affected IDs, Undo boundaries, expiry policy and retained separate data. Never infer crash or power-loss recovery from a confirmation screenshot.
modules.kind: Visible safety affordance / recovery execution unverified

modules.title: Archive, pinning and bookmarks
modules.scope: Keep important content reachable without duplicating it
modules.observed: Our Library offers Archive, and home distinguishes Pinned/Others. Source toggles archive/pin on note identities rather than making content copies.
modules.comparison: Obsidian Bookmarks capture is empty. It establishes an entry point, not successful bookmark creation, folder organisation or persistence.
modules.judgment: Archive, pin, tab pin and bookmark are different concepts. The shared criterion is reliable return to important content, not equal label counts.
modules.direction: Keep pinning and Archive; state when global search includes archived content, and avoid teaching a second path that duplicates the same action.
modules.task: Pin a note, archive it, find it globally, restore it and compare a saved Obsidian bookmark task.
modules.acceptance: Check persisted identity/order, scope labels and no accidental duplicate. Bookmark persistence must be newly verified rather than inferred from its empty pane.

modules.title: Undo, redo, editing history and save feedback
modules.scope: Session recovery, retained history and draft durability
modules.observed: Our top bar exposes Undo/Redo. Source explains retained history bounds: up to 50 steps per note, 64 recently edited notes, 16 MiB on disk; it is not exported in portable backups.
modules.comparison: Obsidian snapshots provide a source-text recovery view; not an equivalent guarantee for every rich-object undo or process interruption.
modules.judgment: Distinguish undo history, saved note, recovery snapshot and backup. A visible Saved label cannot prove every external copy is verified.
modules.direction: Keep clear private-save versus copy-pending feedback and safe Back. Do not fix perceived empty space by hiding durability warnings.
modules.task: Edit text/table/image, undo and redo, leave and reopen; repeat after controlled process restart on disposable data.
modules.acceptance: Verify exact rich payload and history matching the saved revision; preserve current content when history is invalid or trimmed. Never run destructive migration on the user library.

modules.title: Workspaces, tabs and mobile navigation
modules.scope: Notes/Doc, switching contexts, Back and layout restoration
modules.observed: Our Library and Notes/Doc switcher support different destinations; workspace recall is an expert concern, not evidence two workspaces are inherently wrong.
modules.comparison: Obsidian tab overview and Manage workspace layouts are visible. Saving/restoring a layout was not semantically certified, and mobile settings expose additional navigation variants.
modules.judgment: Two different navigation architectures both need a simple return path. Do not demand a desktop-style tab model for our app.
modules.direction: Preserve deliberate Notes/Doc switching and block accidental workspace swipes during drag. Keep route and cursor/scroll context on Back.
modules.task: Switch between two notes, a PDF and Settings; reorder content near an edge, then return to the initial editing location.
modules.acceptance: Log wrong destinations, lost context, accidental switches and state after restart. Workspace restoration is outstanding until a matching live task succeeds.

modules.title: Settings, commands, quick actions and help discovery
modules.scope: Find an action without memorising hidden gestures
modules.observed: Our settings are grouped and globally searchable. The inspected scope does not establish a full action-command palette equivalent; this is not a claim settings search is missing.
modules.comparison: Obsidian command palette, quick action and mobile-toolbar configuration are visible. Slash-command invocation was blocked and keyboard shortcuts do not guarantee touch reachability.
modules.judgment: The gap is discovering the right action at the right time, not simply matching the number of command rows.
modules.direction: Make common actions predictable in context, preserve readable labels and teach rare gestures progressively; evaluate command search only if tasks justify it.
modules.task: Without a walkthrough, find move, undo, export, a setting and one uncommon editor action using touch alone.
modules.acceptance: Observe search terms, wrong taps and help requests; distinguish disabled/contextual/unconfigured actions. Do not use all 205 inventoried commands as a usability success count.

modules.title: Export, sharing, duplication and note composition
modules.scope: PDF/JSON/text, content copy versus flattening, merge safety
modules.observed: Our PDF sheet exposes writing-guide export choice. Source Android text sharing uses plainText with a 100,000-character cap; merging moves sources to Trash and provides Undo.
modules.comparison: Obsidian note-composer commands are inventoried, not a matched full compose/export/share acceptance run. Do not equate a command entry with a successful destination write.
modules.judgment: Different export routes preserve different things. Users need to know when they are sending plain text, a visual PDF, an editable note file or a recoverable backup.
modules.direction: State preservation scope before export, keep originals unchanged, retain per-content copy semantics and verify destination writing rather than reporting chooser launch as completion.
modules.task: Share a mixed note, export PDF and JSON, duplicate it, merge selected notes and undo the merge.
modules.acceptance: Check text/media/table fidelity for each promised format, exact source IDs and retained source copies; destination failure must not silently destroy content.

modules.title: Local summary and text assistance
modules.scope: Extractive summary with source context, not generative AI
modules.observed: NotesController.quickSummary uses a local sentence ranker and displays a warning that it may miss important details. The selected editor frame is context only, not a captured summary result.
modules.comparison: No equivalent built-in summarizer was established in the Obsidian audit. Community AI plugins are outside the installed-core comparison.
modules.judgment: This app-specific tool receives no comparative feature credit. Effectiveness must be judged against faithful extraction and useful coverage, not generated-looking text.
modules.direction: Keep local-only, non-generative labelling, source context and explicit user review. Do not claim a language model or training where none is used.
modules.task: Summarize varied notes with negation, dates and multilingual sentences; check the retained source and decide whether the result is useful.
modules.acceptance: Verify each sentence comes from the source, essential cautions are not lost and limits are clear. No summary-quality test was executed in this report.

modules.title: Privacy, permission boundaries and diagnostic logs
modules.scope: Offline processing, opt-in collection, export and delete
modules.observed: Diagnostics collection is visibly off in the retained frame; the log viewer states there are no matching records. The app manifest declares microphone, notifications and boot reception, not INTERNET.
modules.comparison: Obsidian has accounts/Sync and community-plugin trust boundaries. This does not imply ordinary local editing uploads content or that it is insecure.
modules.judgment: Our local/opt-in stance is worth preserving. A friendly sentence is not a complete privacy/security audit, especially when handing files to another reader.
modules.direction: Keep collection off until opted in; distinguish local save/export from upload and explain external-reader control. Never collect private content merely to make a diagnostic report fuller.
modules.task: Deny microphone, use notes normally, enable logs for a dummy issue, filter/export/delete and inspect the resulting local file.
modules.acceptance: Verify opt-out, readable levels/time range, explicit delete confirmation and exported content minimisation. Security of all native dependencies was not certified here.

modules.title: Smoothness, speed, footprint and reliability
modules.scope: Cold start, typing, drag, file open, search, crashes and memory
modules.observed: The signed APK receipt is 155,195,444 bytes; the verified Obsidian APK is 14,511,986 bytes. Our retained report explicitly has physical_acceptance=false and recognition targets not all met.
modules.comparison: APK size ratio is about 10.7:1, not installed storage, memory, startup latency or a causal explanation of bugs. A static Obsidian reading frame cannot establish a speed winner.
modules.judgment: Your complaints of sluggishness/bugs remain unresolved inputs. No new app-crash count, task latency, jank trace or matched user completion rate was measured.
modules.direction: First define common fixtures and success criteria. Separate bundled-model payload from startup/interaction work; do not trade away offline features solely to chase a tiny APK.
modules.task: On matched hardware, cold start, create/type, search a large library, drag a distant card, open a large PDF and recover from a controlled failure.
modules.acceptance: Collect touch-to-visible timings, frame trace, dropped frames, memory and exact failure logs. Distinguish timeouts/socket failures from app crashes and do not publish a fabricated global score.
modules.kind: Measured APK payload only / live performance unknown

modules.title: Core modules, community plugins and extensibility
modules.scope: Enable/disable, configuration burden and trust
modules.observed: Our inspected app bundles first-party tools; an Obsidian-equivalent user-installable plugin marketplace is not established in this scope.
modules.comparison: Obsidian core toggles and community-plugin warning are visible. The audit records 29 internal module definitions, 28 exposed controls; editor-status is not an extra exposed toggle.
modules.judgment: Plugins change functionality and risk, not automatically UX quality. Missing a third-party extension is not a core-app defect in this comparison.
modules.direction: Keep default flows usable without setup. Treat optional complexity and code execution as separate consent decisions, not onboarding requirements.
modules.task: Find a core module, understand its description, enable/disable it and identify changed controls; inspect restricted/plugin trust text without installing unknown code.
modules.acceptance: Verify reversible configuration and a stable default note workflow. No community code was installed or executed; unknown plugins and future modules are outside this pinned-version inventory.
modules.kind: Version-pinned module census / no plugin execution

modules.title: Sync, Publish, account and service boundaries
modules.scope: Local-first use versus optional cross-device/public services
modules.observed: MyNotes explicitly presents itself as local/no-account. No matching built-in multi-device sync or publishing service was established.
modules.comparison: Obsidian Sync sign-in is visible; Publish was disabled in the retained module inventory. Account/payment-dependent behavior was not executed or accepted.
modules.judgment: These are optional service-scope differences, not evidence that Obsidian synchronises perfectly or our local notes are empty/defective.
modules.direction: Do not bolt on cloud services to win a feature table. Explain local storage, backup and transfer clearly; assess a service only if the product requirement changes.
modules.task: For a future explicitly authorised service study, evaluate offline edits, conflicts, account loss, export and deliberate public visibility with disposable data.
modules.acceptance: No login, purchase, upload or publishing was performed. Conflict resolution, encryption, recovery and cost/value remain untested; an entry screen is not a passed sync task.

modules.title: Slides, presentation and reading projections
modules.scope: View a note as a presentation without changing its source
modules.observed: Our PDF export and PPTX text extraction are different operations from presenting a Markdown note. No equivalent built-in slide-show workflow is established.
modules.comparison: Obsidian shows a Slides title screen, but the software keyboard occupies much of the viewport. This captured constraint prevents claiming a polished full-screen presentation session.
modules.judgment: Presentation is a separate output job. Do not count PPTX extension support as presentation editing or a title screen as successful end-to-end presenting.
modules.direction: For current shared output tasks prioritise readable exports. If presentation becomes required, validate full-screen entry, controls, source preservation and return state.
modules.task: Present a multi-slide disposable note, navigate, dismiss the keyboard, rotate and return to editing; compare PDF reading only as a separate output route.
modules.acceptance: Verify every slide, media, controls and return location. Obsidian landscape was not qualified by its retained audit; no physical presentation run occurred here.
modules.kind: Different output scope / visible comparator viewport constraint

modules.title: About, models, licences and honest help
modules.scope: Version identity, offline model claims and troubleshooting guidance
modules.observed: Our About/model source describes bundled OCR/speech, optional experimental adaptation, disk/RAM costs and separate audio export. This is implementation disclosure, not a new training or accuracy result.
modules.comparison: Obsidian General/settings exposes version/help/account and licences. The inspected screenshot reference pins 1.15.0/code396 rather than claiming all future versions behave alike.
modules.judgment: Help should answer how to do a task before presenting internal engine detail. Existing limitations must stay available, not disappear in a cosmetic simplification.
modules.direction: Keep concise task-first help and progressive technical/licence detail; show exact version and actionable permission/storage recovery routes.
modules.task: Ask a novice to identify where notes are saved, how to protect audio and how to export useful diagnostics without sending private notes.
modules.acceptance: Observe whether they can explain the result in their own words. Do not substitute long notices or a generated guide for successful comprehension.
